title: Vector Database Scaling (Pinecone/Milvus)
summary: Scale vector retrieval by separating storage, indexing, query capacity, tenancy, and ingestion while measuring recall under real constraints.
overview: Vector database scaling is a capacity and correctness problem across several dimensions: vector count, dimensionality, metadata size, query rate, update rate, and filter selectivity. Approximate nearest-neighbor indexes trade search work and memory for recall. Adding replicas may increase read capacity, while sharding changes data distribution and query fan-out.

Managed and self-operated systems expose different operational boundaries, so capacity planning must use the selected product’s behavior rather than assume interchangeable guarantees. Consistency, index readiness, deletion visibility, and metadata filtering affect application correctness. A successful upsert acknowledgment does not necessarily mean every subsequent search immediately sees the change.

production.poc: A prototype uses representative vectors and metadata rather than a tiny unfiltered sample.
production.production: Production benchmarks recall and tail latency under concurrent reads, writes, and selective filters, then sets capacity and freshness objectives.
production.scale: Enterprise scale introduces tenant placement, hot-partition handling, rebuild planning, disaster recovery, and cost models covering replicas, storage, and re-embedding.

components.name: Ingestion workers
components.role: Validate vectors and metadata and write versioned records idempotently.

components.name: Index partitions
components.role: Distribute vector and scalar data across storage and compute boundaries.

components.name: Query replicas
components.role: Provide search capacity with explicit health and index readiness.

components.name: Routing layer
components.role: Selects tenant partitions and merges results across required shards.

components.name: Capacity telemetry
components.role: Tracks latency, recall samples, memory, ingestion lag, and hot partitions.

flow.title: Profile the workload
flow.description: Measure vector sizes, metadata cardinality, query shapes, and update frequency.

flow.title: Choose partitioning
flow.description: Align tenant isolation and expected access patterns while avoiding oversized hotspots.

flow.title: Build and validate indexes
flow.description: Check dimensions, metric choice, and recall against an exact-search sample.

flow.title: Serve constrained queries
flow.description: Route to relevant partitions and apply supported filters with bounded fan-out.

flow.title: Scale the bottleneck
flow.description: Add read replicas, rebalance partitions, or tune indexes according to observed pressure.

flow.title: Rebuild safely
flow.description: Create a new index version, validate it, and switch routing with a rollback path.

useCase.title: Scaling a multilingual product knowledge index
useCase.situation: A marketplace assistant searches product specifications across many sellers and frequent catalog updates.
useCase.problem: A few large sellers create hot partitions while promotions increase query volume and update traffic.
useCase.requirement: Maintain scoped retrieval quality without letting one seller consume the whole search tier.
useCase.architecture: Tenant-aware routing combines partition limits, read replicas, and versioned ingestion checkpoints.
runtime: A query targets only authorized seller partitions.
The platform monitors selective-filter latency and splits an oversized partition after validating the new placement.
useCase.failure: If a new index revision lags or loses recall, routing returns to the previous validated revision.
useCase.impact: Measure recall, p95 search latency, index visibility lag, and cost per workload class; raw vector count does not determine required capacity alone.

tradeoffs.cost: Increase fan-out, merging, and operational complexity.
May lose relevant evidence, especially under selective filters.

failures.detection: Tenant-specific latency diverges from fleet averages.
failures.recovery: Apply quotas and repartition with controlled migration.

failures.detection: Writes fail or incompatible vectors coexist.
failures.recovery: Use a separate versioned index and explicit routing migration.

mistakes.fix: Include real ACL and metadata predicates.

mistakes.mistake: Scaling replicas to fix ingestion bottlenecks

mistakes.fix: Build and validate a parallel index before switching.

whenToUse: Use for growing corpora or sustained concurrent retrieval.
Use when tenant skew affects latency.
Use when updates and queries need separate capacity planning.
whenNotToUse: Avoid distributed indexing for a small stable corpus without need.
Do not assume immediate read visibility after writes.
Do not trade away recall without downstream evaluation.
checklist: Measure recall against an exact baseline.
